title: Sermones Ad Fratres In Eremo Commorantes Et Quosdam Alios [Incertus]
author: Augustine
source: Translated by Claude from stoa0040.stoa013a.opp-lat1, as held by Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina.

passages.original: sola voce paupertatem et abstinentiam prædicant, sed digite saunon cogitaut ea movere : corpora aforis despectis vestibus legunt, sed intus ad carnem purpura induuntur : in cinere praedicam se jacere, sed excelsa, palatia non despiciunt : angelicam faciem aforis osteadunt, sed lupinam eos intus babere non dubitamus. Tales fuerunt illi Sarabaitæ, de quibus tertio nobis scripsit pater Hieronymus, quorum genus est omni affectu vitandum. Ipsi dcnique in Ægypto ciant, in foraminibus petrarum habitantes , iuti porcorum et boum pellibus tantum, cincti funibus palmarum , spinas ad calcanea portantes ad cingulum ligatas, discalceali, sanguine cruentati cavernas exeuntes.
passages.english: They preach poverty and abstinence with their voice alone, but they do not think to move it with [even] a finger; outwardly they cover their bodies with despised garments, but inwardly, next to the flesh, they are clothed in purple; they proclaim that they lie in ashes, but they do not despise lofty palaces; outwardly they show an angelic face, but we do not doubt that inwardly they have a wolf's. Such were those Sarabaites about whom father Jerome wrote to us thirdly, a kind that must be shunned with all our heart. They indeed [lived] in Egypt, dwelling in the holes of rocks, clothed only in the skins of pigs and oxen, girded with ropes of palm, carrying thorns down to their heels tied to their belts, barefoot, coming out of their caves stained with blood.
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: 'digite saunon cogitaut' read as 'digito suo non cogitant'; 'legunt' as 'tegunt'; 'praedicam' as 'praedicant'; 'osteadunt' as 'ostendunt'; 'babere' as 'habere'; 'dcnique' as 'denique'; 'iuti' as 'induti'; 'discalceali' as 'discalceati'. 'ciant' is unclear, perhaps 'erant' ('were'). 'tertio' ('thirdly' or 'a third time') is uncertain in sense.

passages.original: Legimus (n) enim, fratres charissimi, sanctum patrem Hieronymum Cardinalem fuisse (6) in ecclesia sancti Laurentii martyris : et quia Romanos de avaritia et fœtida luxuria fortiter reprehendebat, ab eia per vestem muliebrem (c), ut jam audistis, eum proclamare in populo voluerunt; sed Deo auxiliante sanctitatis fama minime diminuta , Romam tandem egressus est, et cum Paula et Eustochio, quas in fide Christi nutrierat, earum patre rogate, ut nobis per epistolam scripsit, asper rimam vitam sanctus pater Hieronymus duxit: in tantum, ut neminem legero audiam fidelium modernorum austeriorem fuissc. Itaque, fratres, etiam nos, ut vidistis, mundum deserere voluimus, at ad nemora cum Hieronymo fugere concupivimus, et perseverare secundum apostolicam vitam desideramus: propterea diligenter allendamus ut sancte et juste in eremo convivamus.
passages.english: For we read, dearest brothers, that the holy father Jerome was a cardinal in the church of the holy martyr Lawrence; and because he strongly rebuked the Romans for avarice and foul lust, they wished, by means of a woman's garment, as you have already heard, to denounce him before the people. But with God's help his reputation for holiness was not at all diminished, and at length he left Rome; and with Paula and Eustochium, whom he had nurtured in the faith of Christ, at the request of their father, as he wrote to us in a letter, the holy father Jerome led a most harsh life, so much so that I neither read nor hear of any of the faithful of modern times having been more austere. Therefore, brothers, we too, as you have seen, have wished to forsake the world, and have longed to flee to the woods with Jerome, and we desire to persevere according to the apostolic life. Therefore let us diligently take care to live together holily and justly in the hermitage.
passages.notes: Letters in parentheses (n), (6), (c) are editorial footnote marks, omitted. Corrected 'eia' to 'eis', 'legero' to 'legere', 'at' to 'et', 'allendamus' to 'attendamus'. 'earum patre rogate' read as 'earum patre rogante'; sense uncertain.

passages.original: Prima est misera, quia cruciat : secunda est venenosa, quia necat : tertia est ventosa, quia inflat: quarta nat. Nec mirum , si Christus amator sobrietatis, sodolosa, quia dissimulat : quinta gloriosa, quia coro- brietatem spiritus commendat, cum Epicurus præce-, ptor voluptatis eam commendaverit, dicens,Quam felix paupertas est, si læta est! Super hanc propriam voluntatem offert homo devotus, quod præcipue fit in professione obediendi. Sequitur, fratres, Stravit Abraham asinum, duos pieros secum ducens.
passages.english: The first is wretched, because it torments; the second is poisonous, because it kills; the third is windy, because it puffs up; the fourth is deceitful, because it dissembles; the fifth is glorious, because it crowns. Nor is it surprising if Christ, the lover of sobriety, commends sobriety of spirit, since Epicurus, the teacher of pleasure, commended it, saying: 'How happy poverty is, if it is cheerful!' Above this, the devout man offers his own will, which is done especially in the profession of obedience. There follows, brothers: 'Abraham saddled his ass, taking two servants with him.'
passages.notes: The printed lines are jumbled in the scan: 'quarta [dolosa, quia dissimulat; quinta gloriosa, quia coro]nat' has been reassembled, and 'so-[brietatem]' rejoined. Corrected 'pieros' to 'pueros'. The saying attributed to Epicurus is in fact Seneca's quotation of him.
